we have developed a new class of metallogels that are formed by self-organization of Pt(II) or Au(III) complexes, which have the potential to be used in the development of functional materials for applications in the areas of catalysis, molecular recognition, sensors, and drug delivery.
the supramolecular metalogels derived from platinum(II) complexes are highly stable, and can be used to encapsulate and release guest molecules.
the supramolecular metalgels of platinum(II)- and gold(III)-based complexes with tridentated ligands are promising systems for the development of smart materials.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of supramolecular metal complexes as low-molecular-weight gelators.
the design of low molecular weight organogelators, which are based on the self-assembly of metal complexes.
the synthesis and characterization of novel organogelators and their supramolecular metal complexes and their applications in the fields of materials science, nanotechnology, and catalysis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

metallogels derived form platinum(II) complexes have a more robust structure than those derived from gold(III) and that the metallogels derived of platinum(II)-tridentate ligand systems have a higher thermal stability and a lower melting temperature than the metallogels obtained by the self-assembly of the same complexes with the tridentate ligand.

the metal complexes of the type Pt(II) and Au(III) with tridentate N,N′,N″-ligands are able to form supramolecular gels in organic solvents, which are thermally and photo-chemically stable, and can be easily prepared and purified.
supramolecular metalogels are a promising and exciting area for the development of smart materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
supramolecular gels of platinum(II)- and gold(III)-based organometallic complexes are formed by a combination of metal-ligand coordination and hydrogen bonding.
the supramolecular metalogels derived from these complexes are formed by the self-assembling process of the metal complex and the gelators.

metallogelators are a new class of low molecular weight organogelators, which are capable of self-assembly into 1D nanofibers and 3D networks in solution, and can be used as building blocks for supramolecular materials.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the supramolecular metallohydrogelator systems can be used as a model for the design and synthesis of functional materials.

the metal center plays a crucial role in the gelation process and that the supramolecular metalogelators can be designed to exhibit a variety of interesting properties, such as the self-healing, self-recovery and the ability to form gels in water.
